claims.text: The combination of strength and ductility in high-entropy alloys is caused by formation of a single-phase solid solution.
A single-phase high-entropy-alloy solid solution has a severely distorted lattice.
The random distribution of elements with different atomic radii produces severe lattice distortion.
Severe lattice distortion produces variations in interatomic distances and bond lengths.
Variations in bond lengths produce a wider variety of atomic interactions.
The distorted lattice and associated atomic interactions enhance strength and ductility.
The proposed effect operates at room temperature and elevated temperatures.
Single-phase high-entropy alloys will have greater strength and ductility than traditional alloys with similar composition and processing.
The mechanism is limited to single-phase high-entropy alloys of specific elemental compositions.
The exact relationship between lattice structure and mechanical properties remains incompletely understood.
Similar or superior mechanical properties in a multiphase high-entropy alloy relative to the single-phase alloy would falsify the proposed single-phase explanation.

contradictions.description: The stated prediction uses a traditional alloy as the baseline, whereas the falsification experiment uses a multiphase high-entropy alloy as the comparator. These are different comparisons and need not test the same predicted contrast.
